sentences.text: Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for respondent No.3.
 ORDER

This present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 30.11.2015, passed in Motor Accident Claim case No.471/2013 by 5th Additional MACT, Mandsour.
By the said award, the learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim case and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.3,25,030/- along with the interest of 8% per annum.

2. Factual matrix of the case are that on 19.08.2013 at about 3 O'clock, the appellant and her husband were traveling from Mandsaur to Sanjeet on their Activa Scooter bearing registration No.
MP-14-BC/4060.

While they were on the road, a dumper bearing registration No. RJ-09-GA/6691,
driven by respondent No.1 Shankarlal came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and struck their scooter.
As a result of the collision, the appellant sustained grievous injuries.
Her left leg was fractured and later amputated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3608 2 MA-532-2016 below the knee.
She also suffered hearing loss in her right ear.
She has also sustained the injuries to the back of her head, right knee, and other parts of her body.
Tragically, the unborn child she was carrying also died due to the accident.
At the time of the incident, appellant was working as a teacher at "Apna Ghar, Mandsau r," an orphan care center, earning Rs. 2,000/- per month.
She also earned Rs.3,000/- per month by giving private tuition.
In addition, she contributed to her household by managing domestic work, which she valued at Rs.5,000/- per month.
After the accident, she was unable to continue such activities and had to hire a domestic worker at a cost of Rs.2,000/- per month.

Due to the permanent disability and loss of income caused in the accident,
appellant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs. 49,45,000/-.

3. The claims Tribunal after framing issues, recorded the evidence of the parties and held that the Smt. Anamika vs Shankarlal on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32299551/
1 accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle, which was insured with the respondent no.3/Insurance Company on the unfortunate day.

On account of injuries sustained by claimant, the claims Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.1,81,440/- for permanent disability, Rs.10,000/- for special diet, Rs. 43,590/- for artificial limb,
Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.10,000/- for attendant, Rs.5,000/- for conveyance and Rs.25,000/- for medical bills.
Thus, a total sum of Rs.3,25,030/- has been awarded to the claimant.
Hence, the claimant has filed this appeal for enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.

4. Learned counsel for appellant submitted that the award passed by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3608 3 MA-532-2016 Tribunal is contrary to law.
The compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is on the lower side and the award suffers from inadequacy.

The learned Tribunal below has committed a grave error in failing to grant and properly assess general damages despite the appellant having suffered 70% permanent disability, resulting in amputation of the left leg below the knee, miscarriage of the child in the womb, and total future loss of earning capacity along with severe diminution of bodily integrity.
The Tribunal further erred in not taking into consideration the claimant's monthly income of Rs.10,000/-, earned from teaching, stitching, and household work.
Thus, the impugned award suffers from material irregularities and therefore, same is liable to be modified.
5. Learned counsel for respondent no.3 supported the impugned award stating that the just and proper compensation has been awarded to the claimant, therefore, the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
6. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. It is not disputed in this appeal that respondent no.1 was responsible for causing accident by driving offending vehicle, which was insured with respondent no.3 on the fateful day.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not?
8. Upon perusal of the record and after considering the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties.

this Court finds that the Tribunal has awarded compensation on the lower side,
which warrants interference NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3608 4 MA-532-2016 and consequent enhancement.
7. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court found that the income of the claimant would be Rs.5270/- per months.

The yearly income of the claimant would come to Rs.63240/-.
8.

Therefore, after applying the law laid-down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 4 ACJ 270 and Sarla Verma &
Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Others reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the claimant is entitled to get the compensation as under:-

sentences.text: Head Compensation
Permanent disability

Rs.5270 x 12 = Rs.63,240/-
 Add 40% future prospect

Rs.63240/- + Rs.25296/- = Rs. 88536/-
 Rs.7,52,556/
 applying 17 multiplier.

Rs.88536/- X 17 = Rs.15,05112/-
 50% permanent disability  Rs.7,52,556/-
 Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
Medical expenses for fitting artificial limb Rs.43,590/-
 Attender Rs.10,000/-
 Special diet Rs.10,000/-
 Transportation Rs.5,000/-
 Future treatment Rs.25,000/-

Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that the award passed by the learned Tribunal warrants interference, the appellant is entitled for enhancement for a sum of Rs.5,71,116/-
(Rs.8,96,146/ - Rs.3,25,030/ = NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3608 5 MA-532-2016 Rs.5,71,116/) and the enhanced amount shall also carry same interest as has been awarded by the Tribunal.
Rest of the conditions, as imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

9. In view of the foregoing discussion, the appeal stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-
i.
The respondent no.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against it.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee on the enhanced amount also, if required in the present case, within a period of 15 days from today.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
